# Swing and Rate-of-Closure D-Plane Geometry {#swing-rate-of-closure-d-plane-exemplar}

## Purpose and Scope

This governed exemplar explains how `swing_sim` computes frame-explicit
three-dimensional D-plane geometry and how Rate of Closure supplies three
distinct rigid-body velocity points to that calculation. It is for developers,
scientific reviewers, and integrators who need to reproduce the equations and
follow every value into code and tests. It covers geometric direction
relationships only. It does not predict ball launch, spin magnitude,
aerodynamic flight, player outcome, equipment quality, or an operating
decision. The calculation and rendered artifacts are verified-unapproved.

## Design by Contract

### Preconditions

`analyze_dplane` accepts travel, face-normal, target, and up vectors with
exactly three finite components. Face normal, target, and up must each have
Euclidean norm greater than $10^{-12}$. Target and up must be orthogonal to
absolute dot product $10^{-10}$. The Rate-of-Closure adapter additionally
requires a typed `SimulationRun` with increasing sample times and internally
consistent pose, twist, club, scenario, and inspection-event records.

### Postconditions

Every available direction is normalized and every angle is in degrees. Spin
loft is the principal angle on $[0,180]$. A defined D-plane supplies a unit
normal perpendicular to travel and face. Zero, parallel, antiparallel, and
unprojectable states return explicit status or null fields; they never invent a
plane, horizontal heading, or face-to-path result.

### Invariants

A common proper rotation of travel, face, target, and up preserves spin loft,
planar spin loft, face-to-path, and intrinsic tilt. Reflecting the right axis
reverses signed horizontal relationships while preserving spin loft.
Multiplying a nonzero travel vector by a positive scalar does not change the
geometry because only direction enters the method.

## Coordinates, Frames, and Time

### Coordinate Frames

[]{#dplane-coordinate-frame}

The default application frame is
`app_frame:x_target,y_up,z_right`. Let $\hat{\mathbf t}$ be target and
$\hat{\mathbf u}$ be up. The implementation constructs right as

$$
\hat{\mathbf r} =
  \frac{\hat{\mathbf t}\times\hat{\mathbf u}}
       {\lVert\hat{\mathbf t}\times\hat{\mathbf u}\rVert}.
$$

Rate of Closure interpolates the inspection-event rigid transform and twist,
then expresses reference, face-center, and contact vectors in this same frame.

### Axis and Handedness

Positive path and face headings rotate from target toward right. Elevation is
positive toward up. Target-times-up fixes the sign of right; reversing the
cross-product order would reverse every signed horizontal result. The D-plane
normal is travel-times-face, so its orientation also depends on declared order.

### Time Convention

The geometry is instantaneous and has no integration clock. Rate of Closure
evaluates it at `inspection_time_s`. Pose and twist are interpolated to that
event time; the closest sampled index is audit metadata and a bounded tangent
fallback. A miss remains a closest-approach event and is not relabeled impact.

## Units and Dimensions

### Symbol and Unit Table

| Symbol or field | Meaning | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $\mathbf v$ | reference, face-center, or contact velocity | m/s |
| $\hat{\mathbf n}$ | delivered face normal | 1 |
| $\hat{\mathbf t},\hat{\mathbf u},\hat{\mathbf r}$ | target, up, right axes | 1 |
| $\lambda$ | three-dimensional spin loft | degree |
| $p,a,f,\ell$ | path, attack, face, and dynamic-loft angles | degree |
| $\hat{\mathbf d}$ | D-plane normal | 1 |
| `event_time_s` | interpolation time | s |

### Dimensional Checks

Normalizing $\mathbf v$ divides m/s by m/s, producing a unit direction. Dot and
cross products operate on dimensionless directions. `acos` and `atan2`
return dimensionless radians, converted to degrees. The rigid-body equation
$\mathbf v_P=\mathbf v_O+\boldsymbol\omega\times\mathbf r_{OP}$ is consistent:
rad/s is treated as $1/s$, and multiplying by metres produces m/s.

## Derivation and Assumptions

### Assumptions

The calculation assumes Euclidean three-space, a right-handed orthonormal
target frame, finite floating-point inputs, and one instantaneous delivered
face normal. It treats the D-plane as geometry spanned by travel and face;
collision dynamics and aerodynamic response lie outside this method. Rate of
Closure assumes its interpolated homogeneous pose is rigid and its twist stores
angular components followed by translational components.

### Derivation

Normalize travel and face as
$\hat{\mathbf v}=\mathbf v/\lVert\mathbf v\rVert$ and
$\hat{\mathbf n}=\mathbf n/\lVert\mathbf n\rVert$. Their dot product is the
cosine of the included angle. Clipping protects `acos` from roundoff beyond
the mathematical interval.

[]{#dplane-spin-loft-equation}

$$
\lambda = \frac{180}{\pi}
  \cos^{-1}\!\left(
    \operatorname{clip}(\hat{\mathbf v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n},-1,1)
  \right).
$$

When the vectors are not collinear, the oriented plane normal is

[]{#dplane-normal-equation}

$$
\hat{\mathbf d} =
  \frac{\hat{\mathbf v}\times\hat{\mathbf n}}
       {\lVert\hat{\mathbf v}\times\hat{\mathbf n}\rVert}.
$$

For any direction $\mathbf q$, remove its vertical component:
$\mathbf q_h=\mathbf q-(\mathbf q\cdot\hat{\mathbf u})\hat{\mathbf u}$.
Heading and elevation are
$\operatorname{atan2}(\mathbf q_h\cdot\hat{\mathbf r},
\mathbf q_h\cdot\hat{\mathbf t})$ and
$\operatorname{atan2}(\mathbf q\cdot\hat{\mathbf u},
\lVert\mathbf q_h\rVert)$. Face-to-path wraps $f-p$ to $[-180,180)$.
Rate of Closure obtains face-center velocity from rigid-body kinematics before
applying the same geometry.

## Algorithm

### Inputs

The standalone calculation consumes `travel_vector`, `face_normal`,
optional `target` and `up`, and descriptive `frame_id`. The consumer
accepts one immutable `SimulationRun` and derives inspection pose, twist,
shaft geometry, contact lever, face normal, leading-edge tangent, and arc
tangent rather than asking callers to assemble those values.

### Procedure

1. Convert each vector to a finite three-component array and validate the frame.
2. Normalize face, target, and up; derive right from target-times-up.
3. Compute face heading and dynamic loft even if travel is zero.
4. Return `zero_travel` when travel norm is at most $10^{-12}$.
5. Normalize travel; compute path, attack, face-to-path, and spin loft.
6. Return `parallel` or `antiparallel` for a singular cross product.
7. Otherwise derive plane normal, tilt, inclination, and ground intersection.
8. Rate of Closure repeats the calculation for reference, face center, and
   contact so a consumer cannot silently confuse those datums.

Standalone work is constant time and memory. Sector rendering is linear in the
caller-bounded segment count and returns `segments + 1` unit directions.

### Outputs

`DPlaneAnalysis` returns status, frame, normalized basis vectors, optional
plane and ground-intersection directions, three-dimensional and planar spin
loft, residual, path, attack, face, dynamic loft, face-to-path, azimuth, tilt,
and inclination. `ImpactKinematicSnapshot` wraps three analyses with event,
geometry basis, limitations, pose, and wedge-kinematics evidence.

## Implementation Symbols

### Public Symbols

The stable `shared.python.swing_sim.impact` facade exports
`DPlaneStatus`, `DPlaneAnalysis`, `analyze_dplane`, and
`spin_loft_sector_directions`. Rate of Closure exports
`ImpactKinematicSnapshot` and `impact_kinematics_for_run`. Consumers should
not import private helpers such as `_heading_deg` or `_shaft_geometry`.

### Source Mapping

Calculation `TOOLS-DPLANE-GEOMETRY` maps spin loft, normal, heading,
elevation, singular states, and sectors to
`src/shared/python/swing_sim/impact/dplane.py`. The Rate-of-Closure datum and
point-velocity mapping lives in
`src/rate_of_closure/simulation/impact_kinematics.py`. Both are pinned to D3
base `916fb9f27f486486f0c071dcc6f15f81f68ecb18`; their provisional module
IDs and public symbols remain recorded in the module inventory.

## Error and Failure Semantics

### Error Conditions

Wrong vector shape, non-finite values, zero face/target/up, or a nonorthogonal
frame raises `ValueError`. A non-`SimulationRun` input raises `TypeError`.
Nonincreasing times, zero shaft geometry, zero path fallback, or degenerate
projected leading edge also fail preconditions. These failures are distinct
from valid singular geometry.

### Recovery and Cancellation

Callers recover by correcting source data or frame; the method does not coerce,
interpolate missing vectors, or substitute a default. Valid singular statuses
may be displayed with null fields intact. The synchronous calculation is
bounded and has no external I/O, so it has no mid-operation cancellation seam.
Higher-level cancellation occurs before calls or between complete runs.

## Uncertainty and Sensitivity

### Uncertainty Sources

The implementation does not estimate covariance. Uncertainty can enter through
travel, face orientation, coordinate transform, event interpolation, club
geometry, or the choice of reference versus contact datum. Floating-point
clipping addresses numerical roundoff only; it is not a measurement uncertainty
model. Angles therefore remain model-conditioned rather than observed truth.

### Sensitivity

Small perturbations are smooth away from singular states. Sensitivity rises
when horizontal projection approaches zero because heading becomes undefined,
and when travel and face approach parallel or antiparallel because a small cross
product cannot define a stable normal. The API exposes these limits as null or
typed status; downstream code must not carry forward a prior frame's plane.

## Verification and Validation

### Test Evidence

`test_matches_cross_client_golden_contract` executes three analytical cases
from `dplane_golden_v1.json` at absolute tolerance $10^{-9}$ degree.
Singular-state tests cover zero travel, parallel, antiparallel, vertical
projection, and invalid frames. Rotation and reflection tests pin invariants.
The Rate-of-Closure integration test derives face-center velocity independently
as $\mathbf v_O+\boldsymbol\omega\times\mathbf r$, then proves the consumer
normalizes that value for its face-center D-plane.

### Acceptance Criteria

The exemplar passes only when strict JSON Schema and typed loader agree;
calculation, chapter, module, source, consumer, test, and golden-fixture links
all resolve; the fourteen-section linter and focused tests pass; and HTML,
LaTeX, PDF, and DOCX share the governed semantic digest. This evidence verifies
reproduction, not scientific or publication approval.

## Limits and Applicability

### Validity Range

Finite vectors may have any representable scale, but face and frame axes must
exceed norm $10^{-12}$, and target/up orthogonality must satisfy $10^{-10}$.
Spin loft spans $0$ through $180$ degrees. Signed relationships wrap to
$[-180,180)$. The golden fixture qualifies only its declared cases and
$10^{-9}$-degree tolerance.

### Known Limitations

The method does not compute ball response, impulse, spin rate, lift, drag,
landing, biomechanics, or camera-derived pose. It does not establish that an
external device's axes, timestamps, or face normal match this contract. Rate of
Closure downstream flight currently consumes reference-point translation;
shaft-induced contact velocity remains analysis. The markerless-mocap exemplar
is deliberately absent because TOOLS-M0 issue #4708 and PR #4734 are open and
no markerless module exists on this D3 base. Unmerged content is not promoted.

## Worked Examples

### Example Inputs

The governed `square-descending` fixture supplies
$\mathbf v=(0.9986295347545738,-0.052335956242943835,0)$, with path
$0^\circ$ and attack $-3^\circ$. Its face normal is
$\mathbf n=(0.9781476007338057,0.20791169081775934,0)$, with face
$0^\circ$ and dynamic loft $12^\circ$. Target and up use default unit axes.
The fixture tolerance is $10^{-9}$ degree.

### Example Results

The dot product is $\cos 15^\circ$, so spin loft is $15^\circ$. Dynamic loft
minus attack is $12-(-3)=15^\circ$, making planar residual zero.
Travel-times-face points along right, giving
$\hat{\mathbf d}=(0,0,1)$, tilt $0^\circ$, inclination $90^\circ$, and ground
intersection at $0^\circ$. Status is `defined`. Values come from the
cross-client golden fixture and executable Python test, not renderer-only text.
